metadata.title: TIMSS and PIRLS 2011 User Guide for the Fourth Grade Combined International Database
metadata.venue: TIMSS & PIRLS International Study Center / IEA

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The TIMSS and PIRLS 2011 Fourth Grade Combined International Database includes only students who participated in both TIMSS and PIRLS, so the user guide states that appropriate sampling weights were computed to account for the resulting marginal reduction in sample size. The guide also explains that achievement scores were re-scaled using a multi-dimensional IRT approach to preserve the correlation structure across reading, mathematics, and science, and that international benchmarks and context questionnaire scales were re-scaled for reporting. Because this document is a user guide/data documentation rather than an empirical analysis paper, it does not specify a particular weight variable name (e.g., a W_* field) or whether replicate weights (e.g., BRR/jackknife) are used in downstream analyses. Users are directed to the TIMSS 2011 and PIRLS 2011 user guides and to the IEA IDB Analyzer/SAS/SPSS programs for analysis instructions, implying that analysts should apply the provided sampling weights when producing population-representative estimates.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This document is a user guide describing the structure and scaling of the TIMSS and PIRLS 2011 Combined International Database, not an empirical study that models cognitive achievement outcomes with plausible values. As a result, plausible-value generation/combining and missing-data handling strategies are not specified as part of an analysis pipeline. The guide focuses on how achievement scores and contextual scales are constructed and what files/support materials are available, so PV and missing-data handling are not applicable in the sense required for an ML/empirical extraction.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The combined database includes only students who responded to both TIMSS and PIRLS assessments (fourth grade; Botswana and Honduras administered at sixth grade). The guide reports the total combined database student count and indicates that sampling weights were computed to account for this restriction to the overlap sample.

data.outcome_summary: This user guide documents the TIMSS and PIRLS 2011 Fourth Grade Combined International Database, created by administering TIMSS and PIRLS to the same samples of fourth-grade students in 34 countries plus 3 benchmarking entities (with Botswana and Honduras administered at sixth grade). The combined database contains student achievement data and student, home, teacher, and school context data, and it provides sampling weights appropriate for the overlap-only sample. Achievement scores for reading, mathematics, and science were re-scaled using a multi-dimensional IRT framework with concurrent item calibration to preserve the correlation structure across the three domains, and all three scales are placed on an international mean of 500 and standard deviation of 100. The guide also describes included international benchmark variables and re-scaled context questionnaire scales, including a unified resource-shortages scale. It is documentation-focused and does not present model-based predictive results or benchmarks from an analysis; instead, it points users to the TIMSS/PIRLS user guides and analysis tools for conducting statistical analyses.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This is a data documentation/user guide rather than an empirical research paper, so there is no analytic model, no dependent variable prediction target, and no reported performance metrics. Consequently, fields related to ML techniques, plausible-value handling in an analysis pipeline, missing-data handling in estimation, and structured predictive findings are not populated. The guide’s purpose is to explain database contents, scaling, and available support materials so that analysts can conduct downstream analyses using the provided weights and scores.
